texto:
Hello Jim,
My routine in the Academy starts very early in the morning. Every day, I wake up at 06:00 am. I take a fast shower, then I put on my army combat uniform and go to the Alpatacal Courtyard for line up with my comrades. We have to go to breakfast in the mess hall at about 06:40 am. After that, I have classes from 8 am until 1 pm. I'm very tired during the day but later I have lunch and athletics. I love it so much. After that, in the afternoon we go to the mess hall again for dinner. Finally, I have to go to study one more time until the night. Later we have to form up in the formation are and listen the instructions of my lieutenant or brigadier and go to sleep in the barracks. Tomorrow is a new day again.

evaluacion.justificacion:
## Justification
Content: The student addresses all essential and accessory points of the task. For the daily routine, the student details the schedule from waking up at 06:00 am through classes, meals, formation, and going to sleep. For activities and frequency, the routine is framed by "Every day" and includes specific activities like athletics and classes. Free time is implicitly addressed through athletics and the mention of the daily rhythm. The student also offers an opinion on whether life is hard, stating "I'm very tired during the day", which addresses the reader's question about the difficulty of the academy. The target reader is fully informed. This meets band 5.
Organization: The text follows the expected format by including an appropriate greeting ("Hello Jim"). It is connected and coherent, using basic linking words and cohesive devices ("then", "After that", "later", "Finally") to structure the narrative of the daily routine. Paragraphing and punctuation are generally well handled. This meets band 5.
Language: The student uses everyday and taught vocabulary appropriately ("wake up", "army combat uniform", "Alpatacal Courtyard", "line up", "mess hall", "form up", "barracks", "formation are", "brigadier", "lieutenant"). Simple grammatical forms (present simple) are used with a good degree of control ("Every day, I wake up at 06:00 am", "I have classes from 8 am until 1 pm"). Errors are noticeable ("for line up" instead of "to line up", "formation are" instead of "formation area", "listen the instructions" instead of "listen to the instructions") but meaning can still be determined. This meets band 5.

## Target grammar
The student successfully controls the present simple tense and time references ("Every day, I wake up at 06:00 am", "I have classes from 8 am until 1 pm", "we go to the mess hall again for dinner").

Scores: Content 5 | Organization 5 | Language 5
